title: domain-librarian ubiquitous-language library
description: The project's recorded Ubiquitous Language, organized by bounded context. The domain-librarian has sole write custody; humans review and edit under the same rules. Every term carries a definition, and a term lives in exactly one context. Every entity lives under its aggregate, and every invariant lives under the term that enforces it. Aliases point at the canonical term. Unresolved classifications are written as questions, never guessed.

version.description: Document version. This library accepts version 1 only.

project.description: The name of the software whose domain the file records.

description.description: The domain in a few sentences, as the people in it would tell a newcomer.

contexts.description: The bounded contexts in play, a map keyed by context name; one model each.

additionalProperties.description: A description of a boundary, typically a subsystem or the work of a particular team, within which a particular model is defined and applicable. The boundary is set explicitly in terms of team organization, usage within specific parts of the application, and physical manifestations such as code bases and database schemas.

relations.description: The context map: the relations between the recorded contexts, each upstream first.

items.description: One point of contact on the context map, a relationship between an upstream context, whose actions affect the downstream context's success, and a downstream context, whose actions do not significantly affect the upstream. Its kind is one of the published relationship patterns.

context.description: A description of a boundary, typically a subsystem or the work of a particular team, within which a particular model is defined and applicable. The boundary is set explicitly in terms of team organization, usage within specific parts of the application, and physical manifestations such as code bases and database schemas.

definition.description: What the context is responsible for and which model it holds.

aggregates.description: The context's aggregates, each with its identity, member entities, invariants, assertions, repository, and factory.

additionalProperties.description: A cluster of entities and value objects with a boundary around it, treated as a single unit for the purpose of data changes. The one boundary is three things at once. It is a consistency boundary: properties and invariants are defined for the aggregate as a whole, the root enforces them, and inside the boundary consistency rules apply synchronously while across it updates are handled asynchronously. It is a transactional boundary: the aggregate is loaded, saved, and removed whole, one transaction changes one aggregate, and transactions do not cross the boundary. It is a reference boundary: one entity is the root, external objects hold references to the root only, a member's identity is local to the aggregate, and what one aggregate keeps of another is that aggregate's identity.

value_objects.description: Value objects of the context, each with its invariants.

additionalProperties.description: An object that describes or computes some characteristic of a thing and has no conceptual identity: it matters only as the combination of its attributes, two with the same attribute values are equal, and it is treated as immutable, with every operation a side-effect-free function.

A full-fledged part of the domain model representing something that happened in the domain that domain experts care about, as distinct from a system event. It is ordinarily immutable, being a record of the past, and typically carries the time it occurred and the identities of the entities involved.

A standalone operation in the domain for a significant process or transformation that is not a natural responsibility of an entity or value object, declared as an interface with a name that is part of the ubiquitous language and a contract stated as assertions.

A predicate-like value object that tells whether a candidate object matches some criteria, separating the statement of what kind of objects can be selected from the object that does the selecting. It answers through one operation, isSatisfiedBy, and can be combined with other specifications.

questions.description: Open questions about the model, keyed, recorded in place of a guess; a question is never a rule and nothing is enforced from it.

additionalProperties.description: The question, as the team would ask a domain expert.

It is a transactional boundary: the aggregate is loaded, saved, and removed whole, one transaction changes one aggregate, and transactions do not cross the boundary. It is a reference boundary: one entity is the root, external objects hold references to the root only, a member's identity is local to the aggregate, and what one aggregate keeps of another is that aggregate's identity.

Its kind is one of the published relationship patterns.

kind.description:
Relationship kind, one of:
partnership: The two contexts succeed or fail together; the teams coordinate planning and the evolution of their interfaces. Influence runs both ways.
shared_kernel: An explicitly bounded subset of the model, and the code and database design associated with it, that the two teams agree to share and change only in consultation. Influence runs both ways.
customer_supplier: The downstream team is the upstream team's customer; downstream priorities factor into upstream planning and jointly developed acceptance tests validate the interface.
conformist: The downstream team eliminates translation by adhering to the upstream model as it is, sharing the upstream's ubiquitous language.
anticorruption_layer: The downstream context isolates itself with a layer that presents the upstream's functionality in terms of the downstream's own model, translating in one or both directions.
open_host_service: The upstream context defines an open protocol giving access to its subsystem as a set of services, augmented by one-off translators only for idiosyncratic clients.
published_language: The two contexts translate through a well-documented shared language that can express the necessary domain information, often combined with an open-host service.
separate_ways: The two contexts have no connection at all, so each may find simple, specialized solutions within its own scope.

description.description: What passes between the two contexts and which way, in the ubiquitous language.
